title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments
abstract: arXiv:2611.30365v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A Large Language Model (LLM), its harness, and the test-time compute budget jointly determine its behavior. Consequently, the same underlying model, embedded in different agentic workflows or allocated different amounts of test-time compute, can exhibit markedly different performance. Psychologists face an analogous challenge when evaluating human performance: the same person may behave differently under different incentives and levels of deliberation. Psychological tasks therefore provide an ideal testbed for studying such behavioral variation. However, when adapted to LLMs, these tasks are typically text-transcribed, replaying fixed, language-rendered experiments as static prompts. This format is ill-suited to agent evaluation, where actions can alter future observations and task states. Conversely, although dynamic environments are prevalent in the evaluation of LLM agents, they rarely ask whether the resulting behavior is human-like.

translated_title: mini-psych-agent：通过交互式心理环境评估大语言模型智能体的类人行为
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）、其运行框架以及测试时计算预算共同决定了其行为表现。因此，同一个底层模型嵌入不同的智能体工作流程中，或被分配不同的测试时计算资源时，可能会表现出截然不同的性能。心理学家在评估人类表现时面临类似的挑战：同一个人在不同的激励条件和思考程度下可能会有不同的行为。因此，心理学任务为研究这种行为变异提供了理想的测试平台。然而，当这些任务被改编用于LLM时，它们通常被转录为文本形式，即以静态提示词的方式回放固定的、以语言呈现的实验。这种格式并不适合智能体评估，因为在智能体评估中，动作会改变未来的观察结果和任务状态。相反，尽管动态环境在LLM智能体评估中很普遍，但它们很少关注由此产生的行为是否具有类人性。
tldr: 该论文提出mini-psych-agent，一个交互式心理环境测试平台，旨在评估大语言模型智能体在不同智能体工作流程和测试时计算预算下行为表现的类人程度。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces mini-psych-agent, an interactive psychological environment testbed for evaluating the human-likeness of LLM agents' behavior across different agentic workflows and test-time compute budgets.
